source_metadata.title: Characterization of a Catalase-Negative Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Strain
source_metadata.source_type: single clinical isolate characterization / case-report note

batch_manifest.semantic_scope: entire two-page clinical isolate characterization excluding bibliography as evidence

atoms.canonical_statement: The report aimed to molecularly characterize a facultatively anaerobic catalase-negative MRSA isolate identified as Staphylococcus aureus subsp. aureus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We here describe a catalase-negative methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA) isolate that was characterized by amplification and sequencing of the putative catalase gene.

atoms.canonical_statement: The isolate was recovered from tracheal secretion from a 65-year-old multimorbid man admitted to the surgical intensive care unit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 65-year-old male was admitted to the intensive care unit of the Surgery Department of the Mainz University Hospital.

population.label: 65-year-old male surgical ICU patient from whom the isolate was recovered

atoms.canonical_statement: At the time the tracheal secretion was obtained for routine microbiology, the source reported no apparent signs of infection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A tracheal secretion sample was taken for routine microbiological investigation, without signs of any infection being apparent at that time.

population.label: 65-year-old male surgical ICU patient from whom the isolate was recovered

atoms.canonical_statement: The tracheal secretion was processed conventionally, and the isolate underwent repeated catalase testing after aerobic and anaerobic incubation through the fifth subculture.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The tracheal secretion sample was processed conventionally, and creamy beta-hemolytic colonies, typical of S. aureus, were observed on 5% sheep blood agar. The isolate repeatedly tested negative for catalase after either aerobic or anaerobic incubation, even at the fifth subculture.

atoms.canonical_statement: The isolate repeatedly tested catalase-negative yet grew well under both aerobic and anaerobic conditions.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The isolate repeatedly tested negative for catalase after either aerobic or anaerobic incubation, even at the fifth subculture. It grew well both aerobically and anaerobically.

atoms.canonical_statement: Slide coagulase and DNase tests were strongly positive, while BBL CRYSTAL and API Staph identified the isolate as S. aureus with reported probabilities of 98.6% and 97.8%, respectively; 16S rRNA sequencing confirmed S. aureus subsp. aureus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The results of both the slide coagulase test and the DNase test were strongly positive. The BBL CRYSTAL system for gram-positive bacteria (Becton Dickinson Company, Sparks, MD) and the API Staph system (bio-Mérieux, Marcy l’Etoile, France) identified the isolate as S. aureus with 98.6% and 97.8% probabilities (profile codes 0064773465 and 6736153), respectively. DNA sequence analysis of the 16S rRNA gene confirmed the strain as S. aureus subsp. aureus.

atoms.canonical_statement: The strain was deposited in the German Collection of Microorganisms and Cell Cultures as DSM 18827.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This strain was deposited in the DSMZ (German Collection of Microorganisms and Cell Cultures) under the number DSM 18827.

atoms.canonical_statement: Antibiotic susceptibility was determined by disk diffusion on Mueller-Hinton agar using CLSI guidance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Antibiotic susceptibility was determined by disk diffusion on Mueller-Hinton agar based on CLSI (Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute) guidelines.

atoms.canonical_statement: The isolate was resistant to penicillin, oxacillin, cefaclor, cefuroxime, erythromycin, clindamycin, and ciprofloxacin and susceptible to gentamicin, rifampin, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, vancomycin, teicoplanin, and linezolid.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The strain was resistant to penicillin, oxacillin, cefaclor, cefuroxime, erythromycin, clindamycin, and ciprofloxacin but sensitive to gentamicin, rifampin, sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim, vancomycin, teicoplanin, and linezolid.

atoms.canonical_statement: MRSA status was further assessed by PCR targeting mecA and S. aureus-specific genes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The strain was further confirmed as MRSA by using PCR to identify mecA and S. aureus-specific genes as described previously (6).

atoms.canonical_statement: PCR detection of mecA and S. aureus-specific genes further confirmed the isolate as MRSA.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The strain was further confirmed as MRSA by using PCR to identify mecA and S. aureus-specific genes as described previously (6).

atoms.canonical_statement: The catalase gene was amplified by PCR and both strands were sequenced using dye-terminator chemistry on an ABI PRISM 3700 DNA analyzer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The nucleotide sequence of the S. aureus catalase gene in the catalase-negative MRSA strain was amplified by PCR using primers described previously (9), and both strands were sequenced using dye terminator chemistry with an ABI PRISM 3700 DNA analyzer.

atoms.canonical_statement: The catalase-gene sequence of the isolate showed 99.60% identity to katA from MRSA strains Mu50 or N315.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The sequence analysis revealed 99.60% identity to that of the catalase gene katA of MRSA strain Mu50 or N315 (Gen Bank accession no. BA000017 or BA000018, respectively)

concept.text: katA reference sequence from MRSA strain Mu50 or N315

quantitative_result.original_result_text: 99.60% identity to that of the catalase gene katA of MRSA strain Mu50 or N315

atoms.canonical_statement: Relative to Mu50/N315 katA, the isolate differed at six nucleotides: a silent T substitution at position 1152 and a five-base AAACG deletion at positions 1388 to 1392.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: with a difference in 6 nucleotides at positions 1152 and 1388 to 1392 upstream from the initiation codon. The single-base substitution (T) located at bp 1152 upstream from the initiation codon represented a silent mutation. However, deletion of five bases (AAACG) (bp 1388 to 1392 upstream from the initiation codon)

atoms.canonical_statement: The five-base deletion shifted the nucleotide reading frame, replaced downstream amino acids, and caused premature translation termination at bp 1418.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: deletion of five bases (AAACG) (bp 1388 to 1392 upstream from the initiation codon) led to a shift of the nucleotide reading frame, with the consequence of replacement of consecutive amino acids and premature translation termination at bp 1418.

atoms.canonical_statement: The catalase-gene sequence showed 99.54% identity to katA sequences from MSSA476, COL, NCTC 8325, USA300, and MW2, with the same five-base deletion confirmed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Similarly, our catalase gene sequence was 99.54% identical to the katA sequences of S. aureus subsp. aureus strains MSSA476, COL, NCTC 8325, USA300, and MW2, of which complete genomes were also sequenced, with repeated confirmation of the same 5-base deletion.

concept.text: katA reference sequences from MSSA476, COL, NCTC 8325, USA300, and MW2

quantitative_result.original_result_text: 99.54% identical to the katA sequences of S. aureus subsp. aureus strains MSSA476, COL, NCTC 8325, USA300, and MW2

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that the isolate's catalase mutation differed from the katB mutations described in S. aureus subsp. anaerobius but produced the same general consequences: frameshift, early termination, and loss of catalase activity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This mutation thus differed fundamentally from mutations that have been described for the catalase gene katB of catalase-negative S. aureus subsp. anaerobius strains (GenBank accession No. AJ000471) (9). However, the consequences of a deletion in the C-terminal region of catalase seemed to be the same, i.e., a shift of the nucleotide reading frame, an early termination codon, and a loss of the enzymatic activity.

atoms.canonical_statement: The isolate was distinguished from S. aureus subsp. anaerobius and S. saccharolyticus by aerobic growth, clumping-factor expression, acid production from trehalose and lactose, and its 16S rRNA sequence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our strain differs from these species on the basis of its ability to grow well under aerobic conditions, its expression of clumping factor, its production of acid from trehalose and lactose, and its 16S rRNA sequence.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that the clinical relevance of catalase-negative S. aureus strains requires further study.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The clinical relevance of catalase-negative S. aureus strains requires study.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors considered prior reports evidence that catalase is not an absolute requirement for pathogenicity, while allowing that pathogenicity or transmission efficiency could be reduced.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Although few, these reports do provide evidence that catalase is not an absolute requirement for pathogenicity. However, it is possible that pathogenicity or transmission efficiency is decreased.

atoms.canonical_statement: The catalase-negative MRSA strain was repeatedly isolated from the same patient, was not recovered from other ICU or hospital patients, and was not linked to apparent infection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: In our case, the catalase-negative MRSA strain was repeatedly isolated from the same patient but never from other patients of the intensive care unit or the university hospital. There were no indications that the strain had caused an infection.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors inferred from the antibiotic resistance pattern that the catalase-negative strain and other local MRSA strains may have had a common origin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The antibiotic resistance pattern suggested a common origin for the catalase-negative MRSA strain and other local MRSA strains.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors presented the report as the first molecular characterization of a catalase-negative S. aureus subsp. aureus strain.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This is also the first report of a catalase-negative S. aureus subsp. aureus strain characterized with molecular methods.

atoms.canonical_statement: The catalase-gene sequence from the study was deposited in GenBank under accession EF140590.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The catalase gene sequence identified in this study was submitted to GenBank under accession no. EF140590.
